title: Adaptive forms
evidenceStatus: One recorded 81-choice request; all states checked and all 16 complete preference profiles exercised through original callbacks
summary: The recorded policy identifies all eight existing drinks in three questions, matching a deterministic balanced tree. It also recommends a drink for every unsupported complete preference profile because the UI stops at a singleton before confirming unasked constraints. Move exact filtering and question-cost logic into code and use Jev for reviewed language interpretation or ambiguity.
strengths: All menu facts and recorded state choices are inspectable.
Code independently filters candidates and handles completion/conflict.
The UI clearly states that clicks replay one recorded policy.
All eight existing items are identified in three answers, and back navigation restores prior state.

findings.title: Singleton candidates are accepted before unasked hard preferences are checked
findings.evidence: src/journeys.tsx:110 stops at one candidate. Exhaustive callback rollouts give 8/8 existing-item identification but only 8/16 complete-hard-profile compatibility; all eight no-match profiles still receive drinks after three answers.
findings.impact: The form is valid as known-item identification but incomplete as preference elicitation. Unasked properties can violate the visitor's requirements.
findings.fix: Declare task semantics, distinguish unknown from indifferent, confirm remaining requirements and support explicit no-match/relaxation with arbitrary answer editing.

findings.title: The current arithmetic policy has no demonstrated advantage over code
findings.evidence: src/journeys.tsx:58 supplies precomputed matching sets; the best split can be counted exactly. Three questions meet the uniform eight-item information bound. Forty-five terminal choices are overridden by code, and 66 states are unreachable from the default tree.
findings.impact: Successful clicking does not isolate model ability or show reduced effort relative to a deterministic policy.
findings.fix: Use deterministic filtering, stop guards and cost-aware splitting; give Jev language/ambiguity decisions. Display exact policy baselines and distinguish guarded outcomes from raw choices.

findings.title: One non-splitting recorded question is hidden by default reachability
findings.evidence: State s11xx has espresso and latte but chooses sweet; both are unsweetened and dairy is the optimal split. The line-90 guard accepts any unanswered property with multiple candidates. This state is unreachable in the normal tree.
findings.impact: The ordinary demo conceals a real policy mistake and cannot support claims about all 81 decisions from a successful path alone.
findings.fix: Expose all states with split counts, score 35/36 question decisions separately, record any fallback, and version the menu/prompt with the table. Required-property confirmation must use a different criterion from item identification.

simulation.title: A complete preference form with explicit uncertainty
simulation.description: Interpret a free-text request into reviewed hard/soft/unknown preferences, ask useful clarifications, expose unasked requirements before acceptance, handle genuine no-match states and let visitors edit any prior answer.
simulation.jevsRole: Extract source-backed preference strength or choose a bounded clarification for ambiguous wording.
simulation.codeRole: Own menu facts, candidate filtering, legal questions, question costs, stop conditions, conflict sets, history and revision checks.
acceptanceCriteria: No confirmed result violates a hard constraint.
Every no-match case can be inspected and explicitly revised without silently relaxing requirements.
Back/edit preserves consistent history and never repeats an answered question unintentionally.
Late interpretation cannot replace a manual correction or newer menu state.
Completion records full relevant confirmation and separates model choices from code guards.

evaluation.design: Exhaust the current 81 states/16 profiles. Extend to twelve seeded sixteen-item menus with six Boolean attributes: 8748 partial states and 768 profiles. Two input protocols and two order variants yield 34992 choices, packed into 384 requests at 96 questions each. Independently label 24 development/240 held-out utterances; two paraphrases add 480 requests/2880 choices. Total 864 future requests/37872 choices before retries or byte splits. Compare exact code policies and independently checked end outcomes.
baselines: Exact dynamic programming for weighted question cost
Deterministic phrase parser with editable constraints
metrics: Full hard-constraint satisfaction and no-match recall
Known-item identification and best-split correctness separately
Total question cost, unnecessary questions and correction effort
Semantic parse/clarification accuracy and span support
Invalid transitions, stale writes, availability and retry-inclusive latency
Exact finite counts plus menu/utterance-clustered paired intervals

coverage.current: 81 states: 16 conflicts, 29 singletons and 36 multi-candidate states. All actions valid; 35/36 best-split questions and 45/45 terminal labels. Root tree reaches 15 states; 8/8 known items versus 8/16 full profiles succeed.
coverage.full: 12 menus, seeds 42 through 53, with 729 states/64 complete profiles each; 192 feasible and 576 no-match profiles. 864 logical calls/37872 decisions include language evaluation. Offline 1000 action schedules and a proposed 12-person study use frozen outputs.
coverage.feasibility: Fully enumerable authored study; no external dataset or weights. Requires explicit stopping semantics, independently verified facts/language labels and future request budget. Calls and user study were not performed during this audit.

libraries.name: JSON Forms rules
libraries.use: Schema-backed question visibility and enablement, with explicit undefined handling; semantic extraction remains reviewed data.

libraries.name: XState
libraries.use: Represent asking/reviewing/conflict/completed states and guard asynchronous interpretation. Pin a stable version rather than adopting the currently exposed v6 alpha by accident.

nextSteps.action: Declare and report known-item versus full-preference tasks separately.
Add required-property confirmation, explicit conflict relaxation and arbitrary answer editing.
Expose all 81 states and exact best-split comparisons.
Move Jev to reviewed semantic extraction/clarification with version checks.
Bundle menu/state/prompt snapshots and code-guard provenance.
Run exhaustive finite policies and independently labeled language evaluation before effort claims.
